title: Political Prisoner Updates 11.24.26
content:
via NYC ABC

Here is the latest compilation of every-other-week updates:

https://nycabc.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/24-nov-2026.pdf

NYC ABC, along with several other individuals and prisoner support

crews, now send hard copies to all political prisoners and prisoners of

war we support.







If you consistently mail the latest updates to a specific prisoner

please let us know so we can insure there’s no overlap. The goal is to

have copies sent to all of the prisoners we list.

We’ve also been told that some prisoners are not receiving the copies

sent in, yet we aren’t getting rejection notices. If you are in steady

contact with a prisoner, please ask them whether or not they are

receiving the updates and let us know.

Free ’em all,

NYC ABC

title: Make calls for Political Prisoner Xinachtli
content:
Alvaro Luna Hernandez #00255735 is the name and number to use with authorities when calling.




Xinachtli’s held at TDJC-Estelle Unit, experiencing an ongoing medical emergency since late October. He’s been denied access to his doctor, religious counsel, lawyers, and loved ones.

He’s in significant pain and is not receiving adequate medical care.




He’s being denied access to commissary and has been waiting for weeks for a replacement tablet- which broke during a fall. Xinachtli has no walker or wheelchair, and he cannot move without assistance.

He is in isolation.




Xinachtli’s doctor says: “Medically, we are concerned about an acute neurological event that could be life threatening. The TDJC has misled us as to Xinachtli’s whereabouts and his health status despite acknowledging that his private neurologist has a medical release of information and has requested updates.”




Xinachtli and those imprisoned alongside him report that he is barely able to move and his condition is worsening daily.




Rather than comfort and hospice care, the guards have left Xinachtli immobile, in his own excrement, demanding assistance for days on end.




Contact Texas authorities to demand:







Xinachtli’s immediate and unconditional release from prison;




Prompt visitations and communication with religious, legal, medical, family, and friends;




Palliative care and adequate pain

title: Ferguson Political Prisoner Josh Williams released from prison!
content:
We are very thrilled to announce that Ferguson Political Prisoner, Josh Williams, has come home today! This has been a long 11 years being held captive by the state and we are so thankful that he’s finally out and back into community where he belongs.

We wanted to thank all of the groups and individuals that have supported Josh for all these years, this could not have been done without all of your support. We need to continue to support Josh through his transition and we can do so by donating to his re-entry funds and helping him pay off the fees associated with incarceration.

Josh also has another court date coming later in November, so please watch for any announcements regarding support that he might need!




Donate at 

https://givebutter.com/support-ferguson-uprising-political-prisoner-josh-williams-returning-home-sojgqu

title: Why Alex Contompasis deserves Executive Clemency
content:
More than five years have passed since January 6, 2021, a date forever linked with one of the most divisive moments in modern American history.

by Don Ritter (The Saratogian)







While the nation’s attention focused on the attack on the United States Capitol in Washington, D.C., another violent confrontation unfolded hundreds of miles away outside the New York State Capitol in Albany during a “Stop the Steal” rally. It was there that Albany resident Alex Contompasis became involved in a violent altercation that ultimately resulted in his conviction and a lengthy prison sentence.




Today, a striking contradiction exists. Nearly all of the individuals convicted of federal crimes arising from the January 6 events at the U.S. Capitol have been released after President Donald Trump issued sweeping pardons and commutations in January 2025. Yet Alex Contompasis remains incarcerated in New York State. 




Whether one agrees with his politics is not the issue. The real question is whether justice has been served and whether executive clemency is appropriate. Supporters argue that Contompasis believed he was defending himself and others during a rapidly escalating confrontation involving members of the Proud Boys and counter-protesters.
